title: Jean-Jacques Rousseau's birth chart
metaDescription: Jean-Jacques Rousseau's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 6.7° Cancer. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Moon stands at 7.0° Taurus, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 6.7° Cancer: the first decan, whose classical sub-ruler is the Moon. A water sign, read here in its first face.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 15.5° Gemini; Venus stands at 19.9° Gemini; Mars stands at 10.3° Gemini. The tradition reads a mind at home in argument and pattern from Mercury, taste led by wit and proportion from Venus, drive that argues its way forward from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins Uranus and Neptune — a trine holding at 0.5°. Trines are read as inheritance rather than achievement: the ease is genuine, and nothing about it was earned. Behind it, Jupiter square Neptune at 1.2°, and Mars sextile Saturn at 2.2° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Three planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. The Moon in Taurus at 7.0° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mercury in Gemini at 15.5° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Saturn in Leo at 12.5° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 4 earth, 4 air, 1 water, 1 fire by element and 5 mutable, 4 fixed, 1 cardinal by mode. Earth weights a chart toward the material and the durable — what can be built, kept, and relied on. Jupiter was retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Taurus for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.1° between midnight and midnight. The sign survives the missing hour; the degree does not, and is given as a reference rather than a fact. At the noon reference it stands at 7.0°.
